records.people: Raynold Moveni (Deputy Governor, Central Bank of Solomon Islands, appointed 30 January 2020; Chief Manager Financial Systems Regulation Department November 2009-December 2019; CBSI analyst roles from February 1999)
records.move: from the Development Bank of Solomon Islands to the Central Bank of Solomon Islands
records.summary: The Central Bank of Solomon Islands' own board page gives its Deputy Governor a dated banking career before the central bank: Research and Marketing Officer in the Research Department of the Development Bank of Solomon Islands in Honiara from January 1997 to December 1997, then Senior Research and Development Officer in the same department from January 1998 to October 1998, before joining CBSI as a Senior Analyst in February 1999 and rising to Deputy Governor in 2020. The page states no ownership for the Development Bank of Solomon Islands; it is the country's national development bank, so the move is filed as public and is not counted on the layer.
records.detail: Read from the CBSI board of directors page, which publishes dated career lists for all eight board members. Moveni's entry is the only one on the page giving a dated employment outside the central bank with a bank as the employer. The intervening role between CBSI stints was Advisor to the Executive Director at the IMF in Washington DC, September 2007 to October 2009, which is also public. No private-finance employer appears anywhere on the page.

records.people: Luca Beccari (Banca Centrale della Repubblica di San Marino, 10 November 1997 to 8 January 2020, latterly head of the Organisation, Human Resources and General Services Service, 1 April 2019 to 8 January 2020)
records.move: from the Banca Centrale della Repubblica di San Marino to the Secretariat of State for Finance and Budget, and a World Bank consultancy
records.summary: Beccari's own curriculum vitae, published by San Marino's government, gives twenty-two years of dated service inside the central bank and names every outside employer. The outside employers are all public: Coordinator of the Finance and Budget Department at the Secretariat of State for Finance and Budget from 1 January to 30 June 2006 and again from 15 December 2008 to 31 December 2012, both expressly on leave from his central bank post, and a Short Term Consultant post at the World Bank, EDS21. The one private employer on the CV precedes the central bank and is not financial: Exim S.r.l., described on the CV as a San Marino manufacturer and seller of pharmacy furniture and equipment, where he was administrative manager from 1 October 1993 to 30 September 1997.
records.detail: The CV is a three-page Europass document on congressodistato.sm and was read in full. It lists, in order, nine central bank posts from Addetto Area Segreteria e Studi in 1997 through Responsabile Servizio Organizzazione in 2019, with the two ministry secondments and the World Bank consultancy interleaved, and no bank, insurer, asset manager or broker anywhere. He left the central bank on 8 January 2020 to become Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs.

records.people: Benjamin Pereira (former Assistant Governor, Central Bank of Samoa; dates of the central bank posting not given)
records.move: from the Central Bank of Samoa to the Pacific Catastrophe Risk Insurance Company
records.summary: Newsline Samoa reports that the Pacific Catastrophe Risk Insurance Company announced the engagement of the former Central Bank of Samoa Assistant Governor, Benjamin Pereira, to lead Samoa's contingency planning work, in an article of 31 July 2025. The article names no dates for either post and says nothing about who owns PCRIC. The World Bank's own PCRAFI programme paper states that the facility was established in the Cook Islands as a foundation with a board of directors that owns a group captive insurer, and that the Council of Members of that foundation is made up of secretaries of finance from the participating Pacific Island countries, so the employer is publicly owned and the move is filed as public and not counted on the layer.
records.detail: Route taken because the Central Bank of Samoa publishes no career histories: its governor page gives twenty-seven years of unspecified service with no titles or dates, and its board page names only three of five non-executive members with no biographies at all. This record came from searching the career phrase itself, which returned the Newsline Samoa item on a former assistant governor. The ownership question was settled separately from the PCRAFI programme paper on financialprotectionforum.org, pages giving the governance structure.

records.people: Charles Castel (joined the BRH as an advisor to the Governor in 1995; General Counsel, Director of Banking Supervision and General Director, dates not given; Governor from 2007)
records.move: from the Haitian Privatization Commission and a UNDP consultancy to the Banque de la République d'Haïti
records.summary: A World Bank speaker profile for the BRH governor gives his career and names only public employers outside the central bank. It states that he initially joined the BRH as an advisor in 1995, held the posts of General Counsel, Director of Banking Supervision and General Director, and was appointed Governor in 2007. Outside the central bank it names him Executive Director of the Haitian Privatization Commission, where it says he led the government's first successful privatizations, those of the Moulins d'Haiti flour mill and the Cimenterie Nationale cement works, a consultancy for the United Nations Development Program, and teaching posts at the State University of Haiti. No commercial bank, private bank, insurer, asset manager or broker appears anywhere in the profile, and no dates are given for the non-central-bank posts.
records.detail: Reached after the two routes that normally work were tried and failed for Haiti: Sogebank's Rapport Annuel 2023-2024, a 16 MB PDF, publishes only the names of its twelve directors and ten senior managers with no biographies, and Le Nouvelliste's reports on the installation of the 2025 BRH board and on Ronald Gabriel's appointment give names and posts with no prior careers, the latter behind a paywall. The record is filed as public because every outside employer the profile names is a state body, a UN agency or a state university.

records.people: Dr Steve Fanny (Chief Executive Officer of the Seychelles Financial Services Authority; sat on the board of the Central Bank of Seychelles, dates not given)
records.move: from the board of the Central Bank of Seychelles to the board of Nouvobanq and the Seychelles Financial Services Authority
records.summary: The Seychelles Financial Services Authority's own team page for its chief executive states that he sat on various boards including the Central Bank of Seychelles, and lists among the others Nouvobanq, a bank, alongside Indian Ocean Tuna Ltd, the Seychelles Public Transport Corporation, Seychelles Petroleum Company and the Seychelles Investment Board. It also gives earlier public posts as Principal Secretary of Trade in the Ministry of Finance and Special Advisor to the Ministry of Investment, Entrepreneurship Development and Business Innovation. The page gives no dates for any seat and makes no statement about who owns Nouvobanq, which is majority state-held, so the record is filed as public and is not counted on the layer.
records.detail: Filed only after the Central Bank of Seychelles board route was exhausted: of its publicly reported recent directors, Bertrand Rassool's appointment notice carries no employment history, James Jean left the central bank in 2021 for two businesses in agriculture and manufacturing which are private but not financial, and Jean-Paul Barbier is the candidate this project already refused over the 2014-2015 BMI Offshore Bank secondment. This is the first Seychelles career list found that carries both a central bank seat and a bank seat for one person.

blanks.note: TKM: two searches, one in English for the Central Bank of Turkmenistan's chairman, board and management pages and one in Russian for the same (Центральный банк Туркменистана правление руководство биография), return no career list of any kind. The bank publishes no governor, board or management biographies; everything returned is trade-press reporting of dismissals (centralbanking.com items on the chairman being sacked in 2002, replaced by a former deputy, and ousted again) plus Wikipedia. The one biography that exists, centralbanking.com 'Biography of newly-appointed Turkmen c bank chief' of 9 May 2002 on Ymamdurdy Muhammedowic Gandymow, was opened: it gives birth year, the Turkmen agriculture institute 1985-1991 and military service 1986-1988, then truncates at a paywall before naming a single employer. Recommend reclassifying TKM as structurally closed on this row rather than leaving it as a target: no career list is published anywhere, and every Turkmen bank is state-owned, so even a found career would be a public move.

YEM: four career lists read, none giving a central-bank-to-private-finance move. (1) National Bank of Yemen's own CVBoard page, nbyemen.com/iNav/CVBoard_EN.html, read in full: seven dated CVs for chairman, general manager, two deputy GMs and three board members. No one has held a Central Bank of Yemen post; the only central bank link is the CBY Aden nominating Dr Ahmed Ali Omar Bin Sankr as Yemen's representative on the Union of Arab Banks board from 2018, which the page itself calls a nomination and not employment. No board member has a private or commercial bank role. The page also states the bank is 'fully state-owned under the supervision of the Minister of Finance', so even a move there would be public. (2) AGSI profile of Mansour Rageh, CBY deputy governor since 2003: names the Sana'a Center for Strategic Studies, the IFC and Yemen's Social Development Fund, all undated, and no private bank. (3) Wikipedia on governor Ahmed al-Mabaqi: current post and 1983 degree only, no employer. (4) Arab Planning Institute expert CV 5698_162025 (Dr Haitham Qasim Jawas): General Authority for Insurance and Pensions and Aden University, no CBY employment, one 2012 training course at the CBY Aden branch. Al-Amal Microfinance Bank's management page 404s.

SYC: James Jean, appointed to the CBS board effective 1 June 2023, worked at the Central Bank of Seychelles from 2008 to 2021 ending as Head of the Financial Inclusion and Market Conduct Division, then for about two years managed two businesses, one in agriculture and one in manufacturing, which the article does not name. Private but not financial, so logged and not filed, per the row's rule. Source: nation.sc/articles/18112/cbs-board-gets-additional-new-member. Separately confirmed on nation.sc/articles/20653 that outgoing director Bertrand Rassool, on the board 2012-2023, has no employment history published in the appointment notices, and that Jean-Paul Barbier's entry is exactly the BMI Offshore Bank November 2014-June 2015 delegation this project already refused; his current employer is the University of the Sunshine Coast, a public university. Marc Houareau, appointed chairman of Absa Bank Seychelles in September 2022, was also checked: nation.sc/articles/15060 gives him the chairmanship of the Seychelles Pension Fund and an Absa board seat from about 2018 and names no Central Bank of Seychelles post, only CBS approval of his nomination.

SMR: Luca Beccari's CV, read in full and filed above as a public move, carries one private employer and it is not financial: Exim S.r.l., described on the CV as 'Industria sammarinese di produzione e commercializzazione di mobili e attrezzature per farmacie', where he was Responsabile Amministrativo from 1 October 1993 to 30 September 1997, before his central bank service began in November 1997. Logged, not filed, per the row's rule on private but non-financial employers. The lead this project had previously noted, the bluerating.com press profile of a central bank director (bluerating.com/?p=17393, on Giannini's appointment as director of the Banca Centrale), still refuses automated readers: it failed with a client error on WebFetch this round as well.

SLB: the CBSI board page was re-read in full this round and David K.C. Quan's entry still gives 'Deputy Chairman - National Bank of Solomon Islands (NBSI)' with no years, exactly as the earlier round found; his other past involvements, chairmanship of the Solomon Islands National Provident Fund, Solomon Telekom, Solomon Islands Electricity Authority, Solomon Airlines and the Chamber of Commerce, and his managing directorships of AVIS Solomon Islands and Quan Chee Corporation Limited, are equally undated. No dated NBSI role for him was found in any other source and no further calls were spent on him, per instruction. The country was converted instead on a different official, Deputy Governor Raynold Moveni, whose Development Bank of Solomon Islands employment the same page does date.

HTI: Sogebank's Rapport Annuel 2023-2024, the fullest Haitian private-bank document available (sogebank.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Rapport_Annuel-2023-2024.pdf, 16 MB, downloaded and grepped), publishes the names of the Sogebank board and of the boards of Sogebel, Sogecarte, Sogesol, Sogexpress, Fondation Sogebank and Sogeassurance, plus ten 'Hauts Cadres', with no biography for any of them; every occurrence of BRH or 'Banque Centrale' in the document is macroeconomic or regulatory commentary, not a career. Le Nouvelliste's report on the installation of the new BRH board of 11 August 2025 names Ronald Gabriel, Guerly Leriche, Florient Jean Mari, Michèle Delerme and Edwige Jean with no prior careers; its interview with Gabriel on taking office is paywalled before any career detail; centralbanking.com's notice of an earlier BRH board gives five names and posts and nothing else. The country converted on a World Bank speaker profile for an earlier governor instead.

WSM: the Central Bank of Samoa publishes no career history. Its governor page (cbs.gov.ws/about/who-we-are/central-bank-of-samoa-governor) gives the 11 August 2011 appointment and says she has worked at the bank about twenty-seven years in several senior positions, with no titles, dates or outside employer; its board page (cbs.gov.ws/central-bank-of-samoa-board-of-directors) names only three of the five members, Matai'a Alofipo Daniel Meredith, Tuala Pat Leota and Tuala Falani Chan Tung, with no biography and no appointment dates. The country converted on the career-phrase search instead.
